INFR11269 Coursework: individual review 
Each student writes one review of   one assigned submission , independently. The review contributes 
30%   of your coursework mark. Your comments do not determine the reviewed group's mark. 
You will receive the anonymised report and any optional supplementary code. The report's final 
declaration/student - information page will have been removed. You will not receive or assess the 
video. Base your review on the materials provided; executing supplementary code is not required. 
Complete these four fields in Learn 
Field   Maximum 
words   What to include 
Summary   1 5 0   Summarise the question, approach and principal findings in your own 
words. 
Strengths   3 00   At least three distinct, numbered strengths, each explained with 
reference to the work. 
Weaknesses   3 00   At least three distinct, numbered weaknesses or limitations, 
explaining why each matters. 
Detailed Comments   3 00   Develop the most important points into specific suggestions or 
questions that would help the authors improve the work. 
The total maximum is   105 0 words . You do not need to use the full allowance. 
Summary 
Explain what the authors investigated, what they changed and what they found. Distinguish their 
contribution from the supplied system. Keep evaluation of the work for the following fields. 
Strengths 
Identify at least three distinct positive aspects and explain their value. These might concern a clear 
technical decision, a well - controlled comparison, useful evidence, insightful analysis or particularly 
effective presentation. Use page, section, figure or table references where helpful. 
Weaknesses 
Identify at least three distinct weaknesses or limitations. Explain the affected claim or aspect of the 
investigation and why it matters. A weakness may concern experimental coverage, the strength of 
supporting evidence, an unclear explanation or the limits of a conclusion. Distinguish an actual error 
from an unanswered question or a reasonable limitation of scope. 
Detailed Comments 
Prioritise the changes that would most improve the work. Explain what should be changed, clarified or 
tested, and what that would establish. Develop   one or two   important points rather than repeating the 
Strengths and Weaknesses lists. 
For example: 
Figure 3 reports retrieval latency, but the measurement boundary is unclear. Please state whether index 
loading is included. Reporting loading time separately from steady - state search would help readers 
distinguish startup cost from per - query performance. 
This example identifies a specific issue, explains why it matters and proposes an actionable 
improvement.

2 
Writing a useful review 
•   Support comments with specific evidence. Separate observations from assumptions. 
•   Evaluate the work against its stated question and the coursework requirements. Consider both 
system quality and cost where relevant. 
•   Explain why a strength or weakness matters; avoid lists of unexplained labels. 
•   Make constructive, proportionate suggestions. Code is optional, so its absence is not a weakness 
by itself. 
•   Be accurate and respectful. Do not speculate about the authors' identities or motives. 
•   Keep your name, UUN and other identifying information out of the review text; Learn records who 
submitted it. 
The criteria used to mark your review are in   the individual - review rubric . Staff will provide feedback on 
the quality of your review.
